advisories.title: The catch-all calls DR-G17 'inapplicable' without citing the decision that makes it so, and file 08's G17 row does not say that
advisories.finding: closestGateScan's catch-all reason glosses the remaining seventeen gates as 'size, startup, memory, exact-bytes, trust, storage, language quality/runtime, packaging, CI, SARIF (inapplicable), lifecycle, state-class, and ABI/loader'. The parenthetical is a standing claim about another gate. Live file 08 gives DR-G17 the claim 'Every advertised SARIF 2.1.0 projection is a stable, lossless host view of the same applicable result' and the status OPEN — not inapplicable. The characterisation does have a basis in the corpus: file 12 §7 item 3 attributes 'G17-inapplicable' to D-077, and D-077 does record that SARIF drops. But file 12 has no authority, and the artifact cites neither it nor D-077. Everywhere else this artifact sources its claims to quoted cells, which is what makes the one unsourced parenthetical stand out.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: Nothing in the conclusion depends on it. G17 governs the fidelity of a host-side SARIF projection of results that have already been admitted; it does not own refusal at admission, so it fails to own these classes whether or not it is applicable to the preview slice. The reason line's operative sentence — 'None is TypeScript-provider finding/policy/Coverage/planAdmission refusal' — is true of G17 on its own claim text.
advisories.repair: Either drop the parenthetical, or cite it: 'SARIF (inapplicable for analyze per D-077)'. If a later cycle wants to lean on G17's inapplicability for anything load-bearing, it should quote D-077 rather than file 12.

coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with one advisory. Thirteen attacks run, one landed and it is advisory-grade. Read the scope before recording this: what is accepted is a measurement, not a closure. DR-133's leftover-design stays open, the row stays OPEN and not eligible in kind, and D-139's L item for DR-133 is not discharged by this ACCEPT — the artifact says as much itself. All three of my v2 findings land in full. The self-description is rewritten so that authorityClaim and purpose now match the body, the promise to name the later obligation is withdrawn, notNamedHere refuses to assign a live DR-G identifier, claim or harness, and ownsAllSevenNTs — the unsupported assertion that one obligation spans protocol-frame refusal, fact admission, policy, Coverage and planAdmission — is removed rather than argued, which I did not ask for and which improves the artifact. The universal negative is now shown instead of asserted: closestGateScan names five gates including both nearest neighbours I flagged, four of the five claims are byte-exact against the live rows, and the catch-all enumerates the rest — I expanded its ranges programmatically and confirmed that named plus catch-all equals the 22 live gate ids exactly, with nothing missing and nothing invented. The dropped source pin is restored beside the predecessor pin with path, digest, recording and role, and the seven classes still match the contract's negativeTests name for name. Custody is clean throughout: subject unmoved at 0444, v1 and v2 both frozen, each version with its own prompt path, HEAD never left 2d1254e, and all cited digests reproduce. I read all 22 gate claims a third time and affirm the artifact's central negative on my own measurement — no live gate owns host-side relation-registry admission, policy or threshold refusal, Coverage-domain sufficiency, or RequestId allocation. One advisory travels as honesty work: the catch-all calls DR-G17 'inapplicable' without citing D-077, and file 08's G17 row reads OPEN; nothing in the conclusion depends on it, since G17 governs projection of already-admitted results rather than refusal at admission. The next act this artifact identifies — a later D-000 cycle adding a DR-G* obligation with an owner for host-owned provider-output admission — is a D-002 required-gate-set change and is correctly refused here.
